newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to reform fiscal system without tax rise.
newsitem.headline: Japan to reform fiscal system without tax rise.

text.p: The cabinet of Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto has confirmed it will carry out fiscal reforms without raising taxes, Chief Cabinet Secretary Seiroku Kajiyama told a news conference on Wednesday.
Cabinet ministers held the first meeting designed to map out plans to reform Japan's deficit-ridden state fiscal system.

Kajiyama said some cabinet ministers had pointed to the need to activate economic activity while reforming the fiscal system. "Although there are some worries about the economy associated with fiscal reforms, we have no choice but to go ahead with the reform," he said.
In the meeting, Hashimoto reiterated the need to cut government spending without allowing an increase in any spending categories, Kajiyama said.
In the past, the government treated outlays in foreign aid, defence and public works as "sacred categories" which escaped spending cuts.
